newsitem.title: DUBAI: Glaxo Wellcome Saudi sales to start in 96.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome Saudi sales to start in 96.

text.p: A Saudi-British pharmaceuticals plant built in the Red Port city of Jeddah two years ago said on Monday it hoped to start selling its products by end-1996.
Product registration delays and electricity problems, which held up sales by Glaxo Wellcome Saudi Arabia Ltd had been resolved, its general-manager Abid Rawn said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
"Now pricing discussions are ongoing to seek approval for prices of its products in the public sector," he added.
He said the company hoped to market its first batch of products before the end of this year.
Pharmaceutical prices in the kingdom are controlled by the health ministry.
The plant is part of a $26 million joint venture between Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc and the Saudi Import Co.
Factory construction was completed in September 1994, with first output scheduled for mid-1995. But production began only in April 1996 after the factory registration was approved.
The plant aims to meet local consumption needs in Saudi Arabia. The kingdom's population of about 18 million makes it the biggest market in the Gulf.
Glaxo Wellcome products have continued to flow into Saudi Arabia from abroad ahead of sales from the local plant.
It says its business in Saudi Arabia is worth about $46 million annually.

The plant is Britain's first project under Saudi Arabia's Offset Programme, which requires countries winning lucrative defence deals in the kingdom to set up commercial projects which help develop the oil-driven Saudi economy.
